courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: Mandatory Year1 personal and professional development.

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contribution: Direct method: research design, sampling, experimental/survey techniques and descriptive/inferential statistics support developmental and educational inquiry; a general group project is not a teaching placement.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.contribution: Complementary method: data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and an independent data-analysis project supply concrete skills for empirical developmental and educational questions; the datasets are not necessarily educational.

courses.name: The Science of Evolution
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: general evolutionary mechanisms do not supply child-development or orthopedagogical intervention content.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contribution: Complementary normative study: moral theories, responsibility and equality support critical decisions involving children and educational practice; no dedicated Dutch child/education-law syllabus is claimed.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: philosophy of consciousness and personal identity is less directly responsive than qualitative inquiry; replaced.

courses.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: philosophy of emotion is plausible complementary material, but child-inclusive assessment/therapy content strengthens the actual developmental-support core.

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.contribution: Complementary social analysis: institutions, social interaction, inequality, race, gender and class support interpretation of the social environments in which upbringing and learning occur; not sociology of education as a dedicated syllabus.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.contribution: Direct research method: qualitative design, collection, interpretation, reflexivity and group inquiry support the study of educational relationships and practice; topics are not guaranteed to be educational.

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: civil-society theory and NGO research is too indirect for the closest developmental/learning programme; replaced by foundational data methods.

courses.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: general population-health evidence does not establish a distinct24-course orthopedagogy direction.

courses.name: Pharmacology
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: drug targets and pharmacokinetics are not a psychopharmacology or child-treatment syllabus.

courses.name: Infection & Immunity
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: host-pathogen/immune processes are too remote from the defining developmental-support questions.

courses.name: Mechanisms of Disease
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: six-organ pathophysiology does not establish a developmental-support programme.

courses.name: Neurobiology
courses.contribution: Complementary neuroscience: comparative anatomy, biorhythms, animal models, research ethics and experimental laboratory techniques help interpret biological evidence about behaviour; it is not a human child-development course.

courses.name: Perception & Action
courses.contribution: Direct cognitive mechanisms: sensory processing and goal-directed action inform understanding of perceptual/motor functioning; not the comparator’s dedicated child motor-development course.

courses.name: Higher Order Functions
courses.contribution: Direct cognition: memory, emotion, attention, social cognition and experimental reasoning address mechanisms underlying learning and development; the syllabus is not specifically developmental neuropsychology.

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.contribution: Direct cognition/language: acquisition, reading/dyslexia, bilingualism, comprehension and language impairments respond to the target’s cognitive/language and learning questions; not language-teaching didactics.

courses.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
courses.contribution: Complementary biological foundation: cells, inheritance, physiology and cellular communication ground the programme’s study of biological influences on development and prepare for adult physiology; this is not child pedagogy.

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.contribution: Direct foundations: nature–nurture, mental processes, brain function and psychological/neuroscientific methods ground study of typical and atypical development.

courses.name: Molecular Cell Biology
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: general molecular/cell biology does not supply pedagogy, developmental assessment or learning-support content.

courses.name: Human Physiology
courses.contribution: Complementary physiological foundation: adult organ systems, homeostasis, integration, metabolism, growth and ageing support understanding of biological functioning and bodily influences on development; not a paediatric or child motor-development course.

courses.name: Life Science Laboratory
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: blood, bacteria, proteins and DNA laboratory training is biomedical research, not evidence of educational/developmental research training.

courses.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
courses.contribution: Withdrawn: general molecular pathology/genetics is not a sufficiently specific basis for this orthopedagogical concept.

courses.name: Social Psychology
courses.contribution: Direct psychological foundations: theories of social influence on thoughts, feelings and behaviour support analysis of relationships and social development; the course is not child-specific.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.contribution: Direct quantitative method: regression, factor analysis, covariance models and logistic/nonparametric analyses support behavioural evidence and measurement questions; not a complete psychometrics and decision-science course.

courses.name: Abnormal Psychology
courses.contribution: Direct psychopathology: lifespan disorders, developmental pathways, culture, assessment and treatment perspectives include infants, children and adolescents; not specialised orthopedagogical practice.

courses.name: Medical & Health Psychology
courses.contribution: Complementary health psychology: biopsychosocial explanations of stress, health behaviour and chronic illness support analysis of wellbeing and vulnerability across the lifespan, including their consequences for development.

courses.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
courses.contribution: Direct clinical perspective: psychological assessment and psychotherapies across age groups, including children, provide evidence and ethical frameworks for developmental-support questions; no practitioner competence or orthopedagogy qualification is implied.

courses.name: Advanced Research Seminar
courses.contribution: Direct research method: systematic reviews, meta-analysis, effect sizes and R support evidence-based developmental/educational judgments; it synthesises existing studies and does not supply the comparator’s separate primary-research thesis.

courses.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
courses.contribution: Direct developmental core: physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from prenatal life through adulthood, including childhood and adolescence, substantially responds to the target’s defining developmental questions.

courses.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
courses.contribution: Direct, bounded educational application: research and evidence-based materials for youth leaders and educators address democratic school culture, supportive learning environments, empathy and mental wellbeing; not a general special-needs curriculum.

courses.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courses.contribution: Complementary academic skill: argument structure, academic essays and oral presentation support research communication and provide preparation for designing primary-school speaking activities.

courses.name: Rhetoric in Action
courses.contribution: Direct, bounded educational application: students design and teach speaking/debating exercises to primary pupils aged9–12 in a community-engaged course; it is not a full Pabo placement or general didactics sequence.

courses.name: Persuasive Communication
courses.contribution: Complementary communication: framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and persuasion ethics support critical interpretation of influence and responsible public communication about development and learning; the institutional project need not concern schools.
